description: Boundary and logical-path coverage for the identity-predicate dependency constraint, where the forbidden set is phrased as 'types that are <named classes>' rather than passed directly. Behaviourally this constrains the same dependency relation as the direct-named form but emits the predicate-phrased rule sentence. These cases exercise multi-element scopes mixing a violating and a non-violating class, a scoped class that depends on a different target than the headline example, a passing pairing, and multiple forbidden targets at once. The engine renders the quoted predicate rule sentence with one tab-indented '<offending class> does depend on <forbidden class>' line per violation, or the single all-evaluations-passed line otherwise.

cases.expected_output:
"Classes that are "SampleApp.Domain.Order" or "SampleApp.Domain.Customer" should not depend on any types that are "SampleApp.Infrastructure.Database"" failed:
	SampleApp.Domain.Order does depend on SampleApp.Infrastructure.Database

"Classes that are "SampleApp.Services.ReportService" should not depend on any types that are "SampleApp.Data.Repository"" failed:
	SampleApp.Services.ReportService does depend on SampleApp.Data.Repository

"Classes that are "SampleApp.Domain.Order" should not depend on any types that are "SampleApp.Infrastructure.Database" or "SampleApp.Data.Repository"" failed:
	SampleApp.Domain.Order does depend on SampleApp.Infrastructure.Database
